The pine-oak community type is found at elevations from 2,050 to 3,200 feet on less xeric ridges, south-facing slopes, and knobs mainly at higher elevations. The canopy of pines and oaks is much more closed than the previous community, and the shrub layer is also denser. The pitch pine-scarlet oak association of this community occurs at the 2,050 foot elevation, but is best developed above elevation 2,800 feet. Scarlet and chestnut oaks are prominent in this association. The shortleaf pine-oak association is found on steep, south-facing slopes and on ridges below elevation 2,400 feet. Scarlet oak is not prominent in this association.
Several other minor communities are found in the gorges. An alder shrub thicket is found along the river banks. Weedy annuals or young perennials are found on shifting sandbars. Tear-thumb (Polygonum sagittatum, P. persicaria, P. pensylvanicum), velvet grass (Holcus lanatus), bent grass (Agrostis perennans), Panicum spp., and Impatiens capensis are typical. Rocks in the rivers are covered by riverweed (Podostemum ceratophyllum). St. John's wort (Hypericum gentianoides), flax (Linum striatum), beak rush (Rhynchospora glomerata), and yellow-eyed grass (Xyris torta) are found on rock surfaces above the water.
2.2.2 Fauna
The Applicant's Exhibit W may be consulted for lists of fauna found in the Bad Creek area. Golley (1966) and Hall and Kelson (1959) serve as general references to mammals, while Robbins, Bruun, and Zim (1966) and Sprunt and Chamberlain (1970) are useful sources for establishing bird distributions. Hubbs and Lagler (1947), Eddy (1969), and the U.S. Atomic Energy Commission (1972) are useful references for locating the general range of fish species. Ramsey (1956) may be referred to for zoogeographic studies of the fishes of the Savannah River System.
The results of recent fishery investigations in the drainage may be obtained by contacting the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department and the Southeast Reservoir Investigations, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Nomenclature of fishes of the area may be verified by consulting Bailey, et al. (1970).
